projects.title: ReLoop
projects.description: A carbon-aware B2B exchange for surplus packaging. Every match is scored on net CO2e — and the trades that would emit more than they save are suppressed. Built solo for HackOut'26's Circular Carbon Ecosystem theme.

blocks.text: Not every circular trade is worth making.

blocks.body:
Surplus reusable packaging — cardboard, film, pallets, drums, gaylords — ends up landfilled for three reasons. Buyers won't purchase sight-unseen, so trust never forms. Small lots cost more to ship than they're worth, so logistics economics fail. And circularity claims can't be proven, so impact goes unreported.
The key insight: past a distance you can calculate, freight emissions exceed the emissions saved by reuse. Every trade has a carbon break-even radius — and most marketplaces never compute it.
ReLoop was built to make that arithmetic the centre of the product.

blocks.challenge:
Trust: no buyer commits to material they haven't seen.
Economics: small lots are unviable to ship alone.
Impact: circularity claims are unsupportable without data.
blocks.solution:
AI vision grading scores condition (A/B/C/reject) with contamination flags, so material can be trusted sight-unseen.
A matching engine combines hard filters, semantic vectors and a weighted composite score — then the carbon engine scores every match on net CO2e and suppresses carbon-negative trades by default.
Route optimisation (OR-Tools) and 3D bin packing consolidate loads; a hash-chained ledger issues PDF impact certificates.

blocks.captionLeft: Fig. 02 — Dashboard: org and platform CO2e saved

blocks.quote: Every match in ReLoop is scored on net carbon impact, not just price.

blocks.body:
React + TypeScript + Tailwind frontend; FastAPI modular monolith behind it — identity, catalog, grading, matching, carbon, logistics, commerce and reporting services.
PostgreSQL with PostGIS and pgvector powers geo-filtering and the 768-dim semantic search; Redis handles the hot paths. The 3D suite (Flow Globe, Truck Load Studio, Material Passport, Impact Sankey) runs on React Three Fiber.
Everything above was scoped in a full PRD before a line of code — personas, SQL schema, API spec, seed plan and a 3-minute demo script.

blocks.heading: Ranked matches, scored on carbon
blocks.copy:
The matches inbox reads like a ranked feed — match percentage on one side, net CO2e on the other.
Matches past their break-even radius never surface, so the default view is always worth acting on.

blocks.caption: Fig. 04 — Requirements: sourcing streams replace RFPs

blocks.insightText: Break-even radius = ((EF_virgin - EF_reprocess) x load_factor x 1000) / EF_freight. Ship inside it and reuse wins; ship past it and the trade emits more than it saves — so ReLoop hides it.

projects.title: Meridian
projects.description: An institutional-grade, multi-asset portfolio optimization and risk engine. Three quantitative models — Minimum Variance, Markowitz Max-Sharpe and Equal Risk Parity — run over live market data with full backtesting, in milliseconds.

blocks.body:
Retail portfolio tools are black boxes: you get a pie chart, not the mathematics. Meridian flips that — deploy modern quantitative algorithms across equities, commodities and digital assets, and derive mathematically optimal allocations yourself.
The engine compares a 10-asset traditional universe against a 12-asset extended one that includes crypto, so the cost of diversification decisions is visible, not assumed.

blocks.caption: Fig. 01 — Portfolio Builder with universe presets

blocks.challenge:
Optimization results are meaningless without realistic frictions — transaction costs eat theoretical alpha.
Risk numbers without context (Sharpe, Sortino, drawdown) hide what an allocation actually feels like to hold.
Custom allocations had no way to be stress-tested against the optimized ones.
blocks.solution:
Backtests rebalance daily with adjustable transaction costs before reporting CAGR, annualized volatility, Sharpe, Sortino and max drawdown.
A correlation heatmap exposes which assets actually diversify.
Analyze My Portfolio mode takes custom weights and runs live stress tests; Compare Universes puts the 10-asset and 12-asset portfolios side by side.

blocks.captionLeft: Fig. 02 — Results Dashboard: KPI cards and allocations
blocks.captionRight: Fig. 03 — Analyze Portfolio: custom weights under stress

blocks.quote: Derive mathematically optimal allocations via Minimum Variance, Markowitz Max-Sharpe, and Equal Risk Parity.

blocks.body:
FastAPI backend: yfinance data loading with a SQLite TTL cache and CSV fallback, SLSQP-based optimization, Pydantic schemas, and Swagger-documented endpoints — /assets, /prices, /optimize, /backtest, /risk-report, /compare.
React + TypeScript + Vite frontend with custom CSS: GradientMesh, KpiCard and Heatmap components across Builder, Dashboard, Analyze and Compare pages.
The whole stack orchestrates with Docker Compose; the frontend deploys on Vercel.

blocks.insightText: Equal Risk Parity weights the portfolio so every asset contributes equally to total risk — no single position can dominate the outcome.

projects.title: ResilientQA
projects.description: A Playwright-based self-healing test automation framework. When UI changes break a locator, it searches the DOM, ranks candidate elements with rule-based heuristics or a Random Forest ranker, and heals the test in real time.

blocks.body:
Every E2E suite dies the same death: a designer renames a class, an ID becomes a data-attribute, a div gets rewrapped — and half the suite goes red for reasons that have nothing to do with the product being broken.
Teams accept this as maintenance tax. ResilientQA treats it as a ranking problem the framework can solve itself.

blocks.caption: Fig. 01 — The healing pipeline: detect, search, rank, rewrite

blocks.challenge:
A broken locator fails the test and waits for a human to read a stack trace, guess the new selector, and patch it.
Nobody measures how brittle the suite actually is.
blocks.solution:
A HealableLocatorProxy wraps every locator. On failure it parses the live DOM with BeautifulSoup, scores every candidate element with weighted rule-based heuristics (tag, class, text, structural similarity) or a trained Random Forest ranker, and rewrites the locator in real time.
Every heal is logged to SQLite, so suite resilience becomes a metric instead of a feeling.

blocks.alt: Terminal log of a self-healed test run
blocks.caption: Fig. 02 — A locator heals mid-run: candidates ranked, best match rewritten, event logged

blocks.body:
You can't benchmark self-healing on bugs you find by accident. So ResilientQA ships a Synthetic Mutation Engine: it generates diverse broken-UI states — altered IDs, changed classes, reshuffled DOM structure, decoy elements — across 15 different mutation environments.
The mutations double as the training set for the ML ranker; the same environments then benchmark Baseline vs Rule-Based vs ML on Recovery Rate, Precision and Recall.

processSteps.description: mutation_runner.py injects breaks into the Flask demo app and records outcomes.

processSteps.description: The healed/broken pairs train the Random Forest ranker (rf_ranker.joblib).

processSteps.description: 15 synthetic environments compare Baseline vs Rule-Based vs ML.

processSteps.description: Recovery Rate, Precision and Recall land in evaluation reports and charts.

blocks.insightText: Self-healing turns test maintenance into measurement: Recovery Rate, Precision and Recall give a suite a resilience score you can track across releases.

blocks.quote: The framework reads the failure, ranks the DOM, and fixes the test before the run ends.

projects.title: VeriPhi
projects.description: A deep integrity system for the AI era. The Chrome extension scans text as you read, decomposes it into atomic claims, and cross-verifies each one against live search and academic indices — flagging hallucinations with a confidence-gap score.

blocks.text: LLMs sound confident even when they lie.

blocks.body:
Hallucinated facts don't look hallucinated — the prose is fluent, the tone is certain, and nothing on the page tells you which claims have evidence behind them.
Manual fact-checking breaks at reading speed. VeriPhi moves the check into the browser, in real time.

blocks.caption: Fig. 01 — The overlay in action: green = verified, gold = needs citation, red = hallucination risk

blocks.body:
Atomic Decomposition splits AI output into atomic claims using local heuristics.
The Confidence Gap scores each claim: Gap = Linguistic Certainty − Evidence Density. A claim that sounds sure but cites nothing gets flagged — that's the signature of a hallucination.
Cross-Verification sends flagged claims to an orchestrator running real-time queries against Google Search and academic indices.
Source Integrity then ranks what came back: .gov and .edu domains are Gold Tier, generic blogs are Bronze.

blocks.challenge:
Fact-checking tools make you leave the page, paste text, and wait.
Privacy tools that send your whole page to the cloud create the very leak they claim to prevent.
blocks.solution:
The extension injects verdicts into the DOM itself — red, gold and green indicators appear over the claims as you read, no context switch.
PII is scrubbed locally before anything is transmitted; Precision Mode adds strict academic auditing that downgrades any claim lacking a direct citation.

processSteps.title: Score the gap
processSteps.description: Linguistic certainty vs evidence density per claim.

processSteps.title: Rank sources
processSteps.description: .gov / .edu Gold Tier; weak sources Bronze. Verdict overlays render in-page.

blocks.captionLeft: Fig. 02 — The companion site: system init and quick setup
blocks.captionRight: Fig. 03 — The prediction engine, documented step by step

blocks.body:
A Chrome extension (loaded unpacked, Developer Mode) talking to a Node backend on localhost with Gemini Flash 2.5 for claim analysis and Google Search + academic indices for verification — keys live in .env, never committed.
A companion landing site documents the algorithm, modules and the 60-second install path (backend keys, npm start, load unpacked).
Built with Team VectorX — Mehdi Namdar, Jiya Patel, Dev Chauhan and Om Patel.

blocks.insightText: Hallucination detection is a gap problem, not a truth problem — you don't need to know the truth to know that certainty without evidence is the red flag.

projects.title: Autonomous Disaster-Relief Robot
projects.description: An approved conference paper (RIACT) on the design of a fully autonomous robot for disaster management — built to enter rubble, find victims by thermal signature, and deliver food and water until human rescuers can plan a safe mission.

blocks.body:
Earthquakes, landslides, collapsed buildings and mines leave people trapped in rubble — and the site is chaotic, dangerous and time-critical.
Rescuers who enter unknown post-disaster environments face severe injuries from structures nobody has surveyed. The window where victims need food and water most is exactly the window where sending humans is most dangerous.

blocks.caption: Fig. 01 — The robot: two-level mild-steel chassis, rubble-capable wheelbase, conveyor payload deck

items.label: conveyor divisions, grouped by item size
compute boards — Arduino Mega + Raspberry Pi 5

blocks.body:
The chassis is mild steel, 2-3 mm thick, arranged in two levels: motors, wheels, drivers, battery and electronics below; the payload conveyor above. A protection plate under the motors gives 4-5 cm of ground clearance — enough to climb small rubble without damaging the drivetrain.
The conveyor belt carries six divisions separated by wedges, grouped by the size of the items being delivered, controlling the drop rate mechanically. Large wheels and a wide wheelbase carry it through rubble-filled terrain; the drive turns a full 360° on the spot when the mission starts.

blocks.captionLeft: Fig. 02 — Two-level chassis on the bench: motors, wheels and wiring
blocks.captionRight: Fig. 03 — The delivery conveyor with divided payload bays

blocks.body:
An Arduino Mega handles the low level: motors, encoders, ultrasonic sensors and the kill-switch failsafe. A Raspberry Pi 5 runs the autonomy — a thermal camera navigates toward victims by their heat signature, while a camera system streams real-time video and feeds image processing for object identification and environment assessment. The boards talk over UART.
Power is engineered like the rest of the paper: 12 V battery, regulated 5 V rails for both boards, bus bars for organization, and a calculated runtime from measured component and motor power draw.

processSteps.description: The robot enters the rubble zone with zero human intervention.

processSteps.title: Navigate
processSteps.description: Thermal camera locks onto victim heat signatures.

processSteps.title: Assess
processSteps.description: Real-time video and image processing read the environment.

processSteps.title: Deliver
processSteps.description: The conveyor drops food and water packs at controlled rates.

processSteps.title: Hold
processSteps.description: Victims are sustained while rescuers plan a practical, safe mission.

blocks.quote: The robot does the task for the rescuers by entering the area and delivering food and water packs for the victims.

blocks.insightText: Full autonomy is what makes the robot useful — it requires no human intervention at the exact moment when human presence is the most dangerous variable in the equation.
